text:
The silence of the lighthouse is not an absence of sound, but a presence of memory. As the tide rolls in and out, it seems to carry the weight of the past with it. The iron gallery, once a structure of strength, now feels like a skeleton of time. To stand before it is to feel the passage of centuries pressing gently against your own skin.

The keeper's cottage, though cold, holds a warmth that is the warmth of neglect. The slate roof, once a shield against the elements, now sits like a forgotten roof over a sleeping town. The tin of tea on the shelf is a small, fading relic, a reminder that even the most mundane things have a history. It is a tea that once warmed hands that are no longer there, a tea that speaks of a life lived fully before it was left behind.

The maps of the coast, drawn by hand, are a testament to the human desire to understand our own environment. Each line drawn with a notebook and a rope was a promise to remember. The height of the cliffs, the color of the water, the depth of the inlet—all were recorded not just for navigation, but for the soul.
